CHAPTER 9 — काले फलति सौभाग्यम् (KALE PHALATI SAUBHAGYAM)

Introduction — शीर्षकस्य अर्थः (Meaning of the title)

The title काले फलति सौभाग्यम् means 'good fortune bears fruit in its own (proper) time.' काले is the locative (सप्तमी विभक्ति) of कालः (time) — 'in time, at the right time'; फलति (धातु फल्, लट् लकार) means 'bears fruit, ripens'; सौभाग्यम् means 'good fortune, prosperity, welfare'. Just as a mango tree does not fruit the day it is planted but only in its season, honest and sustained effort ripens into success only at the right time. This lesson of NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (Course 309) teaches three linked values: धैर्यम् (patience), उद्योगः (sustained effort) and trust in timely results. It does so through an original story of a patient farmer, five famous public-domain verses on time, patience and gradual progress, and a grammar section drawing सन्धि, समास, विभक्ति and लकार from the very words of the chapter.

कथा — धीरसेनस्य आम्रोद्यानम् (The story: Dhirasena's mango orchard)

आसीत् सुक्षेत्रनामके ग्रामे धीरसेनः नाम कृषकः। एकदा सः अचिन्तयत् — 'मम क्षेत्रे आम्रवृक्षाणाम् उद्यानं रोपयामि। वृक्षाः काले एव फलिष्यन्ति' इति। सः शतम् आम्रबीजानि भूमौ अरोपयत्। प्रतिदिनं प्रातःकाले सः जलं सिञ्चति स्म, तृणानि अपनयति स्म, वृक्षान् पशुभ्यः रक्षति स्म।

तस्य प्रतिवेशी चपलः नाम अपरः कृषकः आसीत्। सः अपि बीजानि अरोपयत्, किन्तु सः अधीरः आसीत्। सप्ताहे सप्ताहे सः भूमिं खनित्वा पश्यति स्म — 'मूलानि वर्धन्ते न वा?' इति। एवं पुनः पुनः खननेन तस्य बीजानि नष्टानि अभवन्। ततः सः क्रुद्धः सन् कृषिम् एव अत्यजत्।

ग्रामजनाः धीरसेनम् उपाहसन् — 'हे मूर्ख! पञ्च वर्षाणि यावत् एकम् अपि फलं न भविष्यति। किमर्थं वृथा श्रमं करोषि?' इति। धीरसेनः शान्तः एव उत्तरम् अददात् — 'वृक्षः स्वकाले एव फलति। अहं श्रद्धया प्रतीक्षे, उद्योगं च न त्यजामि' इति।

तृतीये वर्षे ग्रामे अनावृष्टिः अभवत्। कूपाः शुष्काः जाताः। तथापि धीरसेनः प्रतिदिनं दूरस्थायाः नद्याः जलम् आनीय वृक्षान् असिञ्चत्। तस्य हस्तौ व्रणितौ अभवताम्, किन्तु मनः न अकम्पत।

पञ्चमे वर्षे वसन्तसमये सर्वे वृक्षाः पुष्पिताः, ग्रीष्मे च मधुरैः आम्रफलैः पूर्णाः अभवन्। धीरसेनः फलानि ग्रामजनेभ्यः अयच्छत्, चपलाय अपि अददात्, शेषाणि नगरे विक्रीय धनवान् अभवत्। तदा ग्रामजनाः अवदन् — 'सत्यम् उक्तम् — काले फलति सौभाग्यम् इति। धैर्येण उद्योगेन च एव जनः सुखी भवति' इति।

शब्दार्थाः (from the story): कृषकः = farmer; उद्यानम् = orchard; बीजानि = seeds; अरोपयत् = planted; सिञ्चति स्म = used to water; तृणानि = weeds, grasses; प्रतिवेशी = neighbour; अधीरः = impatient; खनित्वा = having dug; उपाहसन् = mocked; वृथा = in vain; प्रतीक्षे = I wait; अनावृष्टिः = drought; शुष्काः = dried up; आनीय = having brought; व्रणितौ = wounded, blistered (dual); पुष्पिताः = blossomed; विक्रीय = having sold; धनवान् = wealthy.

English translation of the story: In a village named Sukshetra there lived a farmer called Dhirasena. One day he thought, 'I shall plant a mango orchard in my field; the trees will fruit in their own time.' He planted a hundred mango seeds and every morning watered them, weeded them and guarded them from animals. His neighbour, a farmer named Chapala, also planted seeds, but he was impatient: week after week he dug up the soil to see whether the roots were growing, and by this repeated digging his seeds were destroyed; angry, he abandoned farming altogether. The villagers mocked Dhirasena: 'Fool! For five years there will not be a single fruit. Why do you labour in vain?' Dhirasena calmly replied, 'A tree fruits only in its own season. I wait with faith, and I do not give up effort.' In the third year there was a drought; the wells dried up, yet Dhirasena daily carried water from a distant river and watered his trees; his hands were blistered but his mind did not waver. In the fifth year, in spring, all the trees blossomed, and in summer they were laden with sweet mangoes. Dhirasena gave fruit to the villagers — to Chapala too — sold the rest in the town and became prosperous. Then the villagers said, 'Truly it is said: good fortune bears fruit in its own time. Only by patience and effort does a person become happy.'

नीतिः (Moral): Impatience uproots its own seeds; patient, sustained effort — continued through drought and mockery — ripens into abundant fruit at the right time.

श्लोकाः — Verses on time, patience and effort (with शब्दार्थ and अन्वय)

1) उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहमुपैति लक्ष्मीः दैवेन देयमिति कापुरुषा वदन्ति ।
   दैवं निहत्य कुरु पौरुषमात्मशक्त्या यत्ने कृते यदि न सिध्यति कोऽत्र दोषः ॥
   शब्दार्थ: उद्योगिनम् = the industrious (man); पुरुषसिंहम् = a lion among men; उपैति = approaches; लक्ष्मीः = fortune, wealth; दैवेन = by fate; देयम् = is to be given; कापुरुषाः = cowards, mean men; वदन्ति = say; निहत्य = having set aside; कुरु = do!; पौरुषम् = manly effort; आत्मशक्त्या = with one's own strength; यत्ने कृते = when effort has been made; सिध्यति = succeeds; कोऽत्र दोषः = what fault is there?
   अन्वय: लक्ष्मीः उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहम् उपैति। 'दैवेन देयम्' इति कापुरुषाः वदन्ति। (त्वं) दैवं निहत्य आत्मशक्त्या पौरुषं कुरु। यत्ने कृते यदि न सिध्यति, (तर्हि) अत्र कः दोषः?
   Translation: Fortune approaches the industrious lion among men; only cowards say 'it will be given by fate.' Set fate aside and perform manly effort with your own strength; if, effort having been made, success still does not come, what fault is there (in you)?
   Moral: Reject fatalism; your duty is wholehearted effort — the fruit will come in its time, and honest failure carries no blame.

2) शनैः पन्थाः शनैः कन्था शनैः पर्वतलङ्घनम् ।
   शनैर्विद्या शनैर्वित्तं पञ्चैतानि शनैः शनैः ॥
   शब्दार्थ: शनैः = slowly, step by step; पन्थाः = the road (is covered); कन्था = the patched garment (is stitched); पर्वतलङ्घनम् = crossing of a mountain; विद्या = knowledge; वित्तम् = wealth; पञ्च एतानि = these five; शनैः शनैः = only very gradually.
   अन्वय: पन्थाः शनैः, कन्था शनैः, पर्वतलङ्घनम् शनैः, विद्या शनैः, वित्तं शनैः — एतानि पञ्च शनैः शनैः (सिध्यन्ति)।
   Translation: A road is covered slowly; a patched cloth is stitched slowly; a mountain is crossed slowly; knowledge comes slowly and wealth comes slowly — these five are achieved only step by step.
   Moral: क्रमशः progress — great things are completed little by little, never in one leap.

3) क्षणशः कणशश्चैव विद्यामर्थं च साधयेत् ।
   क्षणे नष्टे कुतो विद्या कणे नष्टे कुतो धनम् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: क्षणशः = moment by moment; कणशः = particle by particle; विद्याम् = knowledge; अर्थम् = wealth; साधयेत् = one should acquire; क्षणे नष्टे = when a moment is lost; कुतः = whence?; कणे नष्टे = when a grain is lost; धनम् = wealth.
   अन्वय: क्षणशः विद्यां, कणशः च अर्थं साधयेत्। क्षणे नष्टे विद्या कुतः? कणे नष्टे धनं कुतः?
   Translation: One should gather knowledge moment by moment and wealth grain by grain; if the moment is wasted, whence knowledge? If the grain is wasted, whence wealth?
   Moral: Time is the raw material of fortune; small units of time and resource, patiently accumulated, become learning and prosperity.

4) यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण न रथस्य गतिर्भवेत् ।
   एवं पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति ॥
   शब्दार्थ: यथा हि = for just as; एकेन चक्रेण = with one wheel; रथस्य = of the chariot; गतिः = motion; न भवेत् = cannot be; एवम् = likewise; पुरुषकारेण विना = without human effort; दैवम् = destiny; न सिध्यति = does not succeed.
   अन्वय: यथा हि एकेन चक्रेण रथस्य गतिः न भवेत्, एवं पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति।
   Translation: Just as a chariot cannot move on one wheel, so destiny does not succeed without human effort.
   Moral: Fate and effort are the two wheels of life's chariot; waiting for luck without working is like driving a one-wheeled chariot.

5) काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन कालो गच्छति धीमताम् ।
   व्यसनेन च मूर्खाणां निद्रया कलहेन वा ॥
   शब्दार्थ: काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन = in the delight of poetry and learned works; कालः = time; गच्छति = passes; धीमताम् = of the wise; व्यसनेन = in vice/addiction; मूर्खाणाम् = of fools; निद्रया = in sleep; कलहेन = in quarrel; वा = or.
   अन्वय: धीमतां कालः काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन गच्छति; मूर्खाणां (कालः) व्यसनेन निद्रया कलहेन वा (गच्छति)।
   Translation: The time of the wise passes in the enjoyment of poetry and learning; the time of fools passes in vice, sleep or quarrel.
   Moral: Time passes for everyone; सौभाग्य comes to those who fill that passing time with worthy effort.

व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the chapter

(A) सन्धिः. Joins seen in the verses: पुरुषसिंहम् + उपैति → पुरुषसिंहमुपैति (म् joins the following vowel); कालः + गच्छति → कालो गच्छति (विसर्ग-सन्धि: ः + ग → ओ); शनैः + विद्या → शनैर्विद्या and शनैः + वित्तम् → शनैर्वित्तं (विसर्ग → र्); क्षणशः + च + एव → क्षणशश्चैव (विसर्ग → श् before च; च + एव → चैव, वृद्धि-सन्धि); कः + अत्र → कोऽत्र (विसर्ग-सन्धि, the अवग्रह ऽ marking the lost अ); यथा + हि + एकेन → यथा ह्येकेन (इ + ए → ये, यण्-सन्धि); न + अन्यत्र → नान्यत्र (दीर्घ-सन्धि). Splitting these back (सन्धि-विच्छेदः) is an examinable skill.

(B) समासः. पुरुषसिंहः = पुरुषः सिंहः इव — 'a man like a lion', an उपमित कर्मधारय compound; काव्यशास्त्रम् = काव्यं च शास्त्रं च — a द्वन्द्व compound inside the larger काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन; शुभाशुभम् = शुभं च अशुभं च — द्वन्द्व ('good and bad'); पर्वतलङ्घनम् = पर्वतस्य लङ्घनम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष ('crossing OF a mountain'); पुरुषकारः = पुरुषस्य कारः — तत्पुरुष ('human effort'); अनावृष्टिः = न आवृष्टिः — नञ्-समास ('absence of rain, drought').

(C) विभक्तिः. काले — सप्तमी (locative) 'at the right time'; उद्योगिनम्, पुरुषसिंहम् — द्वितीया (accusative), objects of उपैति; दैवेन, आत्मशक्त्या, एकेन चक्रेण, पुरुषकारेण, विनोदेन, व्यसनेन, निद्रया, कलहेन — तृतीया (instrumental) 'by/with'; रथस्य, धीमताम्, मूर्खाणाम् — षष्ठी (genitive) 'of'; and the special construction यत्ने कृते 'when effort has been made' — a सति-सप्तमी (locative absolute), in which the noun and its participle both stand in the locative to mean 'when/while X is done'.

(D) लकाराः and participles. फलति, उपैति, वदन्ति, गच्छति, सिध्यति — लट् लकार (present tense; वदन्ति is प्रथमपुरुष बहुवचन); कुरु — लोट् लकार (imperative, 'do!'); साधयेत्, भवेत् — विधिलिङ् लकार ('one should...'); निहत्य, खनित्वा, आनीय, विक्रीय — indeclinable gerunds ('having done'): खनित्वा takes the क्त्वा suffix, while निहत्य, आनीय and विक्रीय take ल्यप् because their roots carry a prefix (नि + हन्, आ + नी, वि + क्री).

सारांशः (Summary)

The chapter काले फलति सौभाग्यम् weaves one message through story and verse: good fortune is real, but it ripens on its own calendar, and only for those who keep working while they wait. Dhirasena's orchard shows patient daily effort surviving mockery and drought and fruiting in the fifth year, while impatient Chapala digs up his own seeds. The verses supply the theory: fortune seeks the industrious (उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहम्...), great things come step by step (शनैः पन्थाः...), moments and grains must not be wasted (क्षणशः कणशः...), destiny needs the second wheel of human effort (यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण...), and the wise fill passing time with learning (काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन...). The grammar section turns the same lines into practice in सन्धि-विच्छेद, समास identification, विभक्ति (including the सति-सप्तमी of यत्ने कृते), लकाराः and gerunds. Memorise the verses, retell the story, and — like the mango tree — trust your season.

topics.name: काले फलति सौभाग्यम् — Theme of Time and Fortune
topics.description: The meaning of the title — 'good fortune bears fruit in its own time' — and the chapter's central teaching: patience (धैर्य), sustained effort (उद्योग) and trust in timely results, illustrated by the image of a tree fruiting only in its season.

topics.name: कथा — The Story of the Patient Farmer
topics.description: The original story of the farmer धीरसेन of Sukshetra village, who plants a mango orchard, tends it for five years through mockery and drought, and is rewarded in season — contrasted with impatient चपल, who destroys his own seeds by digging them up.

topics.name: श्लोकाः — Verses on Time, Patience and Effort
topics.description: Five public-domain verses with अन्वय and translation: उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहम्..., शनैः पन्थाः..., क्षणशः कणशः..., यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण..., and काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन... — the classical case for effort over fatalism and step-by-step progress.

topics.name: शब्दार्थ — Vocabulary of the Chapter
topics.description: Word meanings from the story and verses: उद्योगी, कापुरुषः, पौरुषम्, शनैः, कन्था, वित्तम्, क्षणः, कणः, धीमताम्, व्यसनम्, कलहः, अनावृष्टिः and related senior-secondary vocabulary.

topics.name: व्याकरणम् — Sandhi, Samasa, Vibhakti and Lakara
topics.description: Grammar drawn from the chapter's own lines: सन्धि-विच्छेद (कालो गच्छति, कोऽत्र, शनैर्विद्या), समास identification (पुरुषसिंहः, शुभाशुभम्, पर्वतलङ्घनम्), विभक्ति including the सति-सप्तमी of यत्ने कृते, and लकाराः (लट्, लोट्, विधिलिङ्) with क्त्वा/ल्यप् gerunds.

topics.name: Translation, Comprehension and Application
topics.description: Translating story passages and verses into simple English, doing अन्वय, answering comprehension questions, and applying the chapter's message of patient effort to study, work and daily life.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: काले फलति सौभाग्यम् — Theme of Time and Fortune
learning_outcomes.description: Explain the meaning of the title काले फलति सौभाग्यम् and the chapter's central theme that patient, sustained effort ripens into good fortune at the right time, like a tree fruiting in season.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: कथा — The Story of the Patient Farmer
learning_outcomes.description: Recall the sequence of events, characters and outcome of the story of धीरसेन and चपल, and quote the story's key sentences.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: श्लोकाः — Verses on Time, Patience and Effort
learning_outcomes.description: Explain each verse of the chapter with its अन्वय, imagery (lion among men, one-wheeled chariot, mountain crossed slowly) and central idea.
Give accurate English word meanings (शब्दार्थ) of Sanskrit words from the story and verses, such as उद्योगी, कापुरुषः, कन्था, वित्तम्, धीमताम् and व्यसनम्.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: काले फलति सौभाग्यम् — Theme of Time and Fortune
learning_outcomes.description: Analyse the moral themes of the chapter — patience versus impatience, effort versus fatalism, wise versus wasted time — and apply them to situations in study and life.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: व्याकरणम् — Sandhi, Samasa, Vibhakti and Lakara
learning_outcomes.description: Perform सन्धि-विच्छेद of joined forms from the chapter (पुरुषसिंहमुपैति, कालो गच्छति, कोऽत्र, शनैर्विद्या) and identify the समास of compounds such as पुरुषसिंहः, शुभाशुभम् and पर्वतलङ्घनम्.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: व्याकरणम् — Sandhi, Samasa, Vibhakti and Lakara
learning_outcomes.description: Identify the विभक्ति of words in the verses (including the सति-सप्तमी construction यत्ने कृते) and the लकार of verb forms such as फलति, कुरु and साधयेत्, and recognise क्त्वा/ल्यप् gerunds.
Translate story passages and verse lines into simple English, construct अन्वय, and answer comprehension questions on the chapter's words, grammar and message.

chapter_summary.title: काले फलति सौभाग्यम् (Kale Phalati Saubhagyam) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (309) summary covers Chapter 9. It explains the theme 'good fortune bears fruit in its own time', retells the story of the patient farmer धीरसेन and the impatient चपल, presents five classical verses on time, patience and effort with their meanings, and collects the chapter's grammar — सन्धि, समास, विभक्ति and लकार.

काले = सप्तमी of कालः, 'at the right time'
Patience + sustained effort + trust in the season
Image: a tree fruits only in season

branches.label: कथा — Story
details: धीरसेन plants a mango orchard, tends it 5 years
Endures mockery and drought without stopping
चपल digs up his own seeds — impatience destroys
Fifth year: blossoms, sweet fruit, prosperity

sections.heading: The title and its teaching
bullets: काले फलति सौभाग्यम् = 'good fortune bears fruit in its own (proper) time'; काले is the locative of कालः, फलति means 'ripens/bears fruit', सौभाग्यम् means 'good fortune'.
The chapter's teaching is threefold: धैर्यम् (patience), उद्योगः (sustained effort) and trust that honest work ripens at the right time.
The governing image is agricultural: a mango tree fruits only in its season, however eager the planter may be.
Senior-secondary reading connects the theme to both निति literature (effort over fate) and daily student life (steady preparation over cramming).

sections.heading: The story of धीरसेन and चपल
bullets: धीरसेन of Sukshetra plants a hundred mango seeds and daily waters, weeds and guards them, answering mockery with 'वृक्षः स्वकाले एव फलति — the tree fruits in its own season.'
His neighbour चपल, impatient, digs up the soil week after week to check the roots, destroys his own seeds and abandons farming in anger.
In the drought year धीरसेन carries water from a distant river daily; his hands blister but his resolve does not waver.
In the fifth year the orchard blossoms and bears sweet fruit; धीरसेन shares it (even with चपल), sells the surplus and prospers — the villagers themselves pronounce the moral काले फलति सौभाग्यम्.
The two farmers personify धैर्य and अधैर्य: the same soil, seeds and rain yield opposite fates because of patience alone.

sections.heading: Verses on effort against fatalism
bullets: उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहमुपैति लक्ष्मीः — fortune approaches the industrious 'lion among men'; only कापुरुषाः (cowards) say 'fate will provide.'
दैवं निहत्य कुरु पौरुषम् — set fate aside and act with your own strength; if effort honestly made (यत्ने कृते) still fails, no blame attaches — कोऽत्र दोषः?
यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण न रथस्य गतिर्भवेत् — destiny without human effort (पुरुषकार) is a chariot on one wheel: it cannot move.
Together these verses argue that waiting for luck is not patience but cowardice; true patience works while it waits.

sections.heading: Verses on gradual progress and the use of time
bullets: शनैः पन्थाः शनैः कन्था... — five things come only step by step: the road, the patched garment, the mountain crossing, knowledge and wealth.
क्षणशः कणशश्चैव... — gather knowledge moment by moment and wealth grain by grain; a wasted क्षण can never be recovered (क्षणे नष्टे कुतो विद्या).
काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन कालो गच्छति धीमताम् — the wise pass time in poetry and learning; fools pass the same time in vice, sleep or quarrel.
The shared logic: time flows for everyone equally; सौभाग्य belongs to those who fill the flow with small, steady, worthy acts.

sections.heading: Grammar from the chapter
bullets: सन्धि-विच्छेद: पुरुषसिंहमुपैति = पुरुषसिंहम् + उपैति; कालो गच्छति = कालः + गच्छति (विसर्ग-सन्धि); कोऽत्र = कः + अत्र; शनैर्विद्या = शनैः + विद्या; क्षणशश्चैव = क्षणशः + च + एव.
समास: पुरुषसिंहः is an उपमित कर्मधारय ('a man like a lion'); शुभाशुभम् and काव्यशास्त्रम् are द्वन्द्व; पर्वतलङ्घनम् is a षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष; अनावृष्टिः is a नञ्-समास.
विभक्ति: काले is सप्तमी; उद्योगिनम् is द्वितीया; दैवेन, आत्मशक्त्या, निद्रया are तृतीया; धीमताम्, मूर्खाणाम् are षष्ठी; यत्ने कृते is a सति-सप्तमी (locative absolute) — 'when effort has been made.'
लकार and gerunds: फलति, उपैति, वदन्ति are लट्; कुरु is लोट्; साधयेत्, भवेत् are विधिलिङ्; खनित्वा is a क्त्वा gerund while निहत्य, आनीय, विक्रीय take ल्यप् after a prefix.

key_takeaways: Good fortune is real but seasonal: काले फलति सौभाग्यम् — it ripens only at the right time, for those who keep working.
धीरसेन's five patient years beat चपल's five impatient weeks: impatience uproots its own seeds.
Fortune approaches the industrious, not the fatalist — उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहमुपैति लक्ष्मीः; only cowards say 'fate will give.'
Destiny needs the second wheel of human effort — यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण न रथस्य गतिर्भवेत्.
All great things come step by step — शनैः पन्थाः शनैः कन्था; gather knowledge क्षणशः and wealth कणशः.
The wise and the foolish receive the same hours; they differ only in how they fill them (काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन vs निद्रया कलहेन).
Grammar anchors: कालो गच्छति (विसर्ग-सन्धि), पुरुषसिंहः (उपमित कर्मधारय), यत्ने कृते (सति-सप्तमी), कुरु (लोट्), साधयेत् (विधिलिङ्).

glossary.definition: Good fortune, prosperity, welfare — the 'fruit' that ripens in its own time for the patient and industrious.
Time; also the right season or proper moment. काले (locative) means 'at the right time'.
Patience, steadiness, fortitude — the virtue personified by the farmer धीरसेन.
Sustained effort, industry, enterprise; उद्योगी is the industrious person whom लक्ष्मी approaches.
'A lion among men' — a courageous, enterprising man; an उपमित कर्मधारय compound (पुरुषः सिंहः इव).
A coward or mean-spirited man; in the verse, the one who says wealth 'will be given by fate.'
Manly effort, personal exertion; what one must do आत्मशक्त्या, with one's own strength.
Fate or destiny; the chapter teaches it succeeds only when joined to पुरुषकार, human effort.
Human effort or initiative — the second wheel without which the chariot of destiny cannot move.
Slowly, gradually, step by step; the adverb repeated in the verse listing five things achieved only gradually.
A patched garment or quilt, stitched together slowly patch by patch — an image of gradual accomplishment.
क्षणः is a moment of time; कणः is a grain or particle — the small units from which knowledge and wealth are built.
Drought, absence of rain (न + आवृष्टिः, a नञ्-समास); the hardship through which धीरसेन kept watering his trees.
The locative absolute construction, e.g. यत्ने कृते 'when effort has been made' — noun and participle both in सप्तमी.
The gerund suffix used instead of क्त्वा when the root has a prefix, e.g. निहत्य, आनीय, विक्रीय.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — काले फलति सौभाग्यम् (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 9)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give explanations in English. Refer to the story and the verses of the lesson where needed.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of the title 'काले फलति सौभाग्यम्', identifying the grammatical form of काले and the root of फलति.
questions.answer: The title means 'good fortune bears fruit in its own (proper) time.' काले is the सप्तमी (locative) singular of कालः — 'at the (right) time'; फलति is लट् लकार of the root फल् — 'bears fruit, ripens'; सौभाग्यम् means 'good fortune'. The sense: like a tree fruiting in season, honest effort ripens into success only at its proper time.
questions.explanation: Tests the theme plus the grammar of the two key words in the title.

questions.question: Describe in 3-4 sentences how धीरसेन cared for his orchard, and how चपल lost his crop.
questions.answer: धीरसेन planted a hundred mango seeds and every morning watered them, removed weeds and guarded the saplings from animals; even in the drought year he carried water daily from a distant river. चपल, however, was impatient — week after week he dug up the soil to see whether the roots were growing, and by this repeated digging destroyed his own seeds; then he angrily abandoned farming.
questions.explanation: The contrast of sustained care versus impatient interference is the heart of the story.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: उद्योगी, कापुरुषः, पौरुषम्, कन्था, वित्तम्.
questions.answer: उद्योगी = industrious person; कापुरुषः = coward / mean man; पौरुषम् = manly effort, personal exertion; कन्था = patched garment, quilt; वित्तम् = wealth.
questions.explanation: Core vocabulary drawn from the two central verses.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद: (a) कालो गच्छति (b) कोऽत्र (c) शनैर्विद्या.
questions.answer: (a) कालो गच्छति = कालः + गच्छति (विसर्ग-सन्धि: ः + ग् → ओ). (b) कोऽत्र = कः + अत्र (विसर्ग-सन्धि; the अवग्रह ऽ marks the elided अ). (c) शनैर्विद्या = शनैः + विद्या (विसर्ग → र्).
questions.explanation: All three joins occur in the chapter's verses.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति and role of each word: काले, दैवेन, मूर्खाणाम्, and explain the construction यत्ने कृते.
questions.answer: काले = सप्तमी (locative) — 'at the right time'; दैवेन = तृतीया (instrumental) — 'by fate'; मूर्खाणाम् = षष्ठी बहुवचन (genitive plural) — 'of fools'. यत्ने कृते is a सति-सप्तमी (locative absolute): both the noun यत्ने and the participle कृते stand in the locative, together meaning 'when effort has been made.'
questions.explanation: Tests case identification plus the senior-secondary locative-absolute construction.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय of 'उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहमुपैति लक्ष्मीः...' (full verse), translate it, and explain how it answers the fatalist.
questions.answer:
अन्वय: लक्ष्मीः उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहम् उपैति। 'दैवेन देयम्' इति कापुरुषाः वदन्ति। (त्वं) दैवं निहत्य आत्मशक्त्या पौरुषं कुरु। यत्ने कृते यदि न सिध्यति, (तर्हि) अत्र कः दोषः?
Translation: Fortune approaches the industrious lion among men; only cowards say 'it will be given by fate.' Setting fate aside, exert manly effort with your own strength; if, effort having been made, success does not come, what fault is there?
Answer to the fatalist: the verse brands passive reliance on fate as cowardice (कापुरुषता). Our duty and power extend only to effort; results belong to time. Since honest effort is blameless even when it fails, there is never a reason to sit idle waiting for दैव.
questions.explanation: Full verse treatment: अन्वय, translation and भाव — the standard senior-secondary pattern.

questions.question: Compare the characters of धीरसेन and चपल, and state what each teaches about the theme काले फलति सौभाग्यम्.
questions.answer: धीरसेन is patient (धीर), industrious and steady: he plans for the long term, works daily, answers mockery calmly ('वृक्षः स्वकाले एव फलति'), and does not stop even in drought — his hands blister but his mind does not waver. चपल is, as his name says, restless and impatient: he wants proof of progress every week, digs up his own seeds, and abandons the work in anger. Both had the same soil, seeds and season; only their attitude to time differed. धीरसेन teaches that trust in the season plus unbroken effort ripens into सौभाग्य; चपल teaches that impatience destroys the very roots of one's own fortune. The theme thus needs both halves: work like धीरसेन, and never interrogate the seed like चपल.
questions.explanation: Character-sketch question mapping each farmer onto one half of the chapter's moral.

questions.question: Translate: 'यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण न रथस्य गतिर्भवेत् । एवं पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति ॥' and state its moral.
questions.answer: Translation: Just as a chariot cannot move on one wheel, so destiny does not succeed without human effort. Moral: fate and effort are the two wheels of life's chariot — luck alone, without work, takes no one anywhere.
questions.explanation: The chariot simile makes दैव and पुरुषकार interdependent.

questions.question: Which five things does the verse 'शनैः पन्थाः शनैः कन्था...' say are achieved only slowly? What is its message?
questions.answer: The five: पन्थाः (the road covered), कन्था (the patched garment stitched), पर्वतलङ्घनम् (the crossing of a mountain), विद्या (knowledge) and वित्तम् (wealth). Message: all great things are accomplished step by step (शनैः शनैः) — gradual, steady progress, not one great leap.
questions.explanation: Recall of the five items plus the meaning of the repetition शनैः शनैः.

questions.question: Identify the समास and give the विग्रह of: पुरुषसिंहः and शुभाशुभम्.
questions.answer: पुरुषसिंहः — उपमित कर्मधारय समास; विग्रह: पुरुषः सिंहः इव ('a man like a lion'). शुभाशुभम् — द्वन्द्व समास; विग्रह: शुभं च अशुभं च ('good and bad').
questions.explanation: Two compound types met in the chapter's grammar section.

questions.question: 'काले फलति सौभाग्यम्' इत्यस्य समुचितः अर्थः कः? (What is the correct meaning of the title?)
options: Good fortune bears fruit in its own time
Good fortune comes instantly to all
questions.answer: Good fortune bears fruit in its own time
questions.explanation: काले (at the right time) फलति (bears fruit) सौभाग्यम् (good fortune).

questions.question: 'काले' इति पदे का विभक्तिः?
questions.explanation: काले is the locative (सप्तमी) singular of कालः — 'at the (right) time'.

questions.question: The chapter's central teaching combines patience and effort with what third element?
options: Trust that results come at the right time
Dependence on the favour of kings
questions.answer: Trust that results come at the right time
questions.explanation: धैर्य + उद्योग + trust in timely results (काल-विश्वास) form the chapter's triad.

questions.question: 'फलति' इति क्रियापदस्य धातुः कः?
questions.explanation: फलति is the लट् (present) form of the root फल्, 'to bear fruit'.

questions.question: The chapter compares the ripening of good fortune to which natural image?
options: A tree fruiting in its season
questions.answer: A tree fruiting in its season
questions.explanation: The governing image is agricultural: however eager the planter, the tree fruits only in season.

questions.question: 'सौभाग्यम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: सौभाग्यम् means good fortune, prosperity, welfare.

questions.question: Besides sustained effort (उद्योग), which quality does the chapter most strongly urge?
questions.explanation: Patience — waiting through the growing season without abandoning work — is the chapter's key virtue.

questions.question: Which attitude is the direct OPPOSITE of the chapter's message?
options: Demanding instant results and quitting when they do not appear
Working daily and waiting for the season
questions.answer: Demanding instant results and quitting when they do not appear
questions.explanation: चपल's impatience — wanting fruit before the season — is the anti-model of काले फलति सौभाग्यम्.

questions.question: कथायां धैर्यशीलस्य कृषकस्य नाम किम्?
questions.explanation: The patient farmer is धीरसेन (from धीर, 'steady, patient').

questions.question: कथा कस्मिन् ग्रामे प्रचलति? (In which village is the story set?)
questions.explanation: The story is set in a village named सुक्षेत्र ('good field').

questions.question: धीरसेनः किं रोपितवान्?
questions.explanation: He planted a hundred mango seeds (शतम् आम्रबीजानि) to raise an orchard.

questions.question: अधीरस्य प्रतिवेशिकृषकस्य नाम किम्?
questions.explanation: The impatient neighbour is चपल (the name itself means 'restless, fickle').

questions.question: चपलस्य बीजानि कथं नष्टानि?
questions.explanation: Week after week he dug up the soil to check the roots; the repeated digging destroyed the seeds.

questions.question: कति वर्षाणि यावत् धीरसेनः फलं प्रतीक्षितवान्? (After how many years did the orchard bear fruit?)
questions.explanation: In the fifth year the trees blossomed in spring and bore sweet fruit in summer.

questions.question: अनावृष्टिकाले धीरसेनः किम् अकरोत्?
options: दूरस्थायाः नद्याः जलम् आनीय वृक्षान् असिञ्चत्
questions.answer: दूरस्थायाः नद्याः जलम् आनीय वृक्षान् असिञ्चत्
questions.explanation: During the drought he daily brought water from a distant river and watered the trees.

questions.question: ग्रामजनाः आदौ धीरसेनं प्रति किम् अकुर्वन्?
questions.explanation: At first the villagers mocked him: 'For five years there will be no fruit — why labour in vain?'

questions.question: उपहासं श्रुत्वा धीरसेनः किम् उक्तवान्?
questions.explanation: His calm reply — 'a tree fruits only in its own season; I wait with faith and do not give up effort.'

questions.question: कथायाः अन्ते ग्रामजनाः किं वाक्यम् अवदन्?
questions.explanation: Seeing the laden orchard, the villagers themselves pronounced the chapter's moral.

questions.question: श्लोकानुसारं लक्ष्मीः कम् उपैति? (According to the verse, whom does Lakshmi approach?)
questions.explanation: उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहमुपैति लक्ष्मीः — fortune approaches the industrious lion among men.

questions.question: 'दैवेन देयम्' इति के वदन्ति?
questions.explanation: Only cowards (कापुरुषाः) say wealth 'will be given by fate.'

questions.question: 'यत्ने कृते यदि न सिध्यति' — ततः किम् इति श्लोकः पृच्छति?
questions.explanation: If effort honestly made does not succeed, 'what fault is there?' — honest failure is blameless.

questions.question: 'शनैः पन्थाः...' श्लोके कति वस्तूनि शनैः सिध्यन्ति इति उक्तम्?
questions.explanation: पञ्चैतानि शनैः शनैः — five things: road, patched garment, mountain-crossing, knowledge, wealth.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT among the five things listed in 'शनैः पन्थाः शनैः कन्था...'?
questions.explanation: The five are पन्थाः, कन्था, पर्वतलङ्घनम्, विद्या and वित्तम्; धैर्यम् is not in the list.

questions.question: 'क्षणशः कणशश्चैव' श्लोकानुसारं किं किं साधयेत्?
questions.explanation: One should acquire knowledge moment by moment and wealth grain by grain.

questions.question: 'क्षणे नष्टे कुतो ____' — श्लोके किं पदम् अस्ति?
questions.explanation: क्षणे नष्टे कुतो विद्या — if the moment is wasted, whence knowledge?

questions.question: रथ-दृष्टान्तेन श्लोकः किं बोधयति? (What does the chariot simile teach?)
questions.explanation: As a chariot cannot move on one wheel, destiny fails without the second wheel of human effort.

questions.question: धीमतां कालः केन गच्छति?
questions.explanation: The time of the wise passes in the delight of poetry and learned works.

questions.question: मूर्खाणां कालः कैः गच्छति इति श्लोके उक्तम्?
questions.explanation: Fools' time passes in vice, sleep or quarrel — the same hours, differently filled.

questions.question: Which is the correct अन्वय of 'उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहमुपैति लक्ष्मीः'?
questions.explanation: लक्ष्मीः is the subject (प्रथमा); उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहम् is the object (द्वितीया) of उपैति.

questions.question: 'पुरुषसिंहः' इत्यस्य भावः कः?
questions.explanation: पुरुषसिंहः = 'a lion among men', a man courageous and enterprising like a lion.

questions.question: 'उद्योगी' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: उद्योगी = one who exerts sustained effort; from उद्योगः, industry.

questions.question: 'उपैति' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: उपैति (उप + इ) = goes near, approaches.

questions.question: 'कापुरुषः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: कापुरुषः = a contemptible or cowardly man — the one who leaves everything to fate.

questions.question: 'पौरुषम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: पौरुषम् = personal exertion, manly effort — what one must do आत्मशक्त्या.

questions.question: 'शनैः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: शनैः = slowly, gradually, step by step.

questions.question: 'कन्था' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: कन्था = a patched cloth or quilt, stitched slowly patch by patch.

questions.question: 'वित्तम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: वित्तम् = wealth, riches (synonym of धनम्).

questions.question: 'धीमताम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: धीमताम् = genitive plural of धीमान् (possessing धी, intellect) — 'of the wise'.

questions.question: 'कलहः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: कलहः = quarrel, strife — one of the ways fools waste time.

questions.question: 'क्षणः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: क्षणः = an instant, a moment of time.

questions.question: 'कणः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: कणः = a grain or particle — wealth is gathered कणशः, grain by grain.

questions.question: 'व्यसनम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: व्यसनम् = a vice or addiction; in the verse, one of the fools' time-wasters.

questions.question: चपलस्य कथा-भागात् कः बोधः लभ्यते? (What lesson does Chapala's part of the story give?)
options: Impatience destroys the roots of one's own success
Seeds must be checked every week
questions.answer: Impatience destroys the roots of one's own success
questions.explanation: By digging up his seeds to check progress, चपल himself destroyed them — impatience is self-defeating.

questions.question: 'उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहम्...' इति श्लोकः कं वादं निराकरोति? (Which attitude does the verse reject?)
questions.explanation: The verse brands 'fate will provide' as the speech of cowards and commands action instead.

questions.question: Which student behaviour best reflects the chapter's teaching?
options: Revising a little every day through the year and trusting the exam season
Cramming the whole syllabus on the last night
Abandoning a subject after one poor test
Waiting for luck to bring good marks
questions.answer: Revising a little every day through the year and trusting the exam season
questions.explanation: Daily steady effort with patience for results is धीरसेन's method applied to study.

questions.question: रथ-दृष्टान्तानुसारं सफलतायाः कृते किं किम् आवश्यकम्?
questions.explanation: Like the two wheels of a chariot, success needs both destiny/time and human effort.

questions.question: 'शनैः शनैः' इति पुनरुक्तिः किं सूचयति?
questions.explanation: The repetition stresses gradualness: great things are completed only step by step.

questions.question: उपहासं प्रति धीरसेनस्य व्यवहारः अस्मान् किं शिक्षयति?
questions.explanation: He answered mockery calmly and stayed at his work — meet ridicule with quiet perseverance.

questions.question: Which English proverb is closest to काले फलति सौभाग्यम्?
options: As you sow, so shall you reap — in due season
Out of sight, out of mind
Too many cooks spoil the broth
questions.answer: As you sow, so shall you reap — in due season
questions.explanation: Sowing (effort) and reaping in due season (timely fruit) mirror the chapter's theme.

questions.question: काव्यशास्त्र-श्लोकानुसारं धीमतां मूर्खाणां च मध्ये मुख्यः भेदः कः?
questions.explanation: Both receive the same hours; the wise fill them with learning, fools with vice, sleep or quarrel.

questions.question: 'पुरुषसिंहमुपैति' इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: The final म् of the accusative joins the following vowel उ.

questions.question: 'कालो गच्छति' इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: विसर्ग-सन्धि: the visarga of कालः becomes ओ before the voiced ग्.

questions.question: 'शनैर्विद्या' इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: The visarga after ऐ becomes र् before the voiced व् (विसर्ग-सन्धि).

questions.question: 'क्षणशश्चैव' इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: Visarga → श् before च; then च + एव → चैव (वृद्धि-सन्धि).

questions.question: 'कोऽत्र' इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: कः + अत्र → कोऽत्र; the अवग्रह (ऽ) marks the elided अ.

questions.question: 'यथा ह्येकेन' इत्यत्र 'ह्येकेन' इत्यस्य विच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: यण्-सन्धि: the इ of हि becomes य् before the vowel ए — हि + एकेन → ह्येकेन.

questions.question: 'पुरुषसिंहः' इति पदे कः समासः?
questions.explanation: पुरुषः सिंहः इव — 'a man like a lion', a कर्मधारय of the उपमित type.

questions.question: 'शुभाशुभम्' इति पदे कः समासः?
questions.explanation: शुभं च अशुभं च — 'good and bad', a coordinating द्वन्द्व compound.

questions.question: 'पर्वतलङ्घनम्' इति पदे कः समासः?
questions.explanation: पर्वतस्य लङ्घनम् — 'the crossing OF a mountain'; the first member is in the genitive relation.

questions.question: 'अनावृष्टिः' इति पदे कः समासः?
questions.explanation: न + आवृष्टिः = अनावृष्टिः, 'absence of rain, drought' — a negative (नञ्) compound.

questions.question: 'उद्योगिनम्' इति पदे का विभक्तिः?
questions.explanation: It is the accusative object of उपैति — whom fortune approaches.

questions.question: 'दैवेन' इति पदे का विभक्तिः?
questions.explanation: दैवेन = 'by fate' — instrumental (तृतीया) singular.

questions.question: 'यत्ने कृते' इति का रचना (construction)?
questions.explanation: Noun and participle both in the locative: 'when effort has been made.'

questions.question: 'मूर्खाणाम्' इति पदे का विभक्तिः किं वचनं च?
questions.explanation: मूर्खाणाम् = 'of fools', genitive plural.

questions.question: 'कुरु' इति क्रियापदं कस्य लकारस्य रूपम्?
questions.explanation: कुरु is the imperative (लोट्) second person singular of कृ — 'do!'

questions.question: 'साधयेत्' इति क्रियापदं कस्य लकारस्य रूपम्?
questions.explanation: साधयेत् = 'one should acquire' — the optative/potential विधिलिङ्.

questions.question: 'फलति' इति क्रियापदं कस्य लकारस्य रूपम्?
questions.explanation: फलति is present tense (लट्), third person singular.

questions.question: 'वदन्ति' इति रूपं कः पुरुषः किं वचनम्?
questions.explanation: वदन्ति = 'they say' — third person (प्रथमपुरुष in Sanskrit ordering) plural, लट्.

questions.question: 'निहत्य' इति रूपे कः प्रत्ययः?
questions.explanation: Because the root हन् carries the prefix नि, the gerund takes ल्यप् (निहत्य), not क्त्वा.

questions.question: 'खनित्वा' इति रूपे कः प्रत्ययः?
questions.explanation: खन् has no prefix, so the gerund takes क्त्वा — खनित्वा, 'having dug'.

questions.question: Choose the correct translation of 'दैवं निहत्य कुरु पौरुषमात्मशक्त्या'.
options: Setting fate aside, perform manly effort with your own strength
Worship fate and wait for its gifts
Fate destroys the effort of the strong
By fate alone does effort succeed
questions.answer: Setting fate aside, perform manly effort with your own strength
questions.explanation: निहत्य = having set aside; कुरु = do!; पौरुषम् = manly effort; आत्मशक्त्या = with one's own strength.

questions.question: Choose the correct translation of 'शनैः पर्वतलङ्घनम्'.
options: A mountain is crossed slowly, step by step
questions.answer: A mountain is crossed slowly, step by step
questions.explanation: पर्वतलङ्घनम् (the crossing of a mountain) happens शनैः — gradually.

questions.question: Choose the correct translation of 'निद्रया कलहेन वा'.
questions.explanation: निद्रया (instrumental of निद्रा) = by sleep; कलहेन = by quarrel; वा = or.

questions.question: Choose the correct translation of 'न रथस्य गतिर्भवेत्'.
questions.explanation: रथस्य गतिः न भवेत् — 'there would be no motion of the chariot' (on one wheel).

questions.question: 'वृक्षः स्वकाले एव फलति' — समुचितः अनुवादः कः?
options: A tree bears fruit only in its own season
A tree bears fruit throughout the year
The tree's fruit falls before its season
questions.answer: A tree bears fruit only in its own season
questions.explanation: स्वकाले = in its own time; एव = only; फलति = bears fruit.

questions.question: The title 'काले फलति सौभाग्यम्' means that good fortune comes instantly to anyone who wishes for it.
questions.explanation: The title says the opposite: fortune bears fruit only in its own proper time, after patient effort.

questions.question: धीरसेनः अनावृष्टिकाले स्वम् उद्यानम् अत्यजत्। (Dhirasena abandoned his orchard during the drought.)
questions.explanation: He did not abandon it — he carried water daily from a distant river and kept the trees alive.

questions.question: चपलस्य बीजानि तस्य स्वस्य पुनः पुनः खननेन एव नष्टानि। (Chapala's seeds were destroyed by his own repeated digging.)
questions.explanation: His impatient checking of the roots destroyed the seeds — impatience defeated itself.

questions.question: According to the verse, लक्ष्मी approaches the lazy man who waits for fate.
questions.explanation: लक्ष्मी approaches the उद्योगी (industrious) पुरुषसिंह; relying on fate is the mark of cowards.

questions.question: The verse 'शनैः पन्थाः...' lists exactly five things that are accomplished only gradually.
questions.explanation: पञ्चैतानि — the road, the patched garment, the mountain-crossing, knowledge and wealth.

questions.question: 'कन्था' इत्यस्य अर्थः 'राजभवनम्' इति। ('कन्था' means 'palace'.)
questions.explanation: कन्था means a patched garment or quilt, not a palace.

questions.question: The chapter rejects pure fatalism — the belief that fate alone, without effort, brings success.
questions.explanation: Both the lion-among-men verse and the chariot verse insist that दैव succeeds only with पुरुषकार.

questions.question: 'कालो गच्छति' इति रूपं विसर्ग-सन्धेः उदाहरणम् अस्ति। ('कालो गच्छति' is an example of visarga-sandhi.)
questions.explanation: कालः + गच्छति → कालो गच्छति; the visarga becomes ओ before the voiced consonant ग्.

questions.question: 'साधयेत्' इति रूपं लोट्-लकारस्य अस्ति। ('साधयेत्' is a form of the imperative लोट्.)
questions.explanation: साधयेत् is विधिलिङ् ('one should acquire'); the लोट् form would be साधयतु.

questions.question: According to 'काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन कालो गच्छति धीमताम्', the time of the wise passes in the enjoyment of poetry and learning.
questions.explanation: That is the verse's first line; fools' time passes in vice, sleep or quarrel.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहम् उपैति ________।
questions.explanation: उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहमुपैति लक्ष्मीः — fortune approaches the industrious lion among men.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — दैवं निहत्य कुरु ________ आत्मशक्त्या।
questions.explanation: दैवं निहत्य कुरु पौरुषमात्मशक्त्या — set fate aside and exert manly effort.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — शनैः पन्थाः शनैः ________ शनैः पर्वतलङ्घनम्।
questions.explanation: The patched garment (कन्था) is the second of the five slow accomplishments.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — क्षणे नष्टे कुतो ________।
questions.explanation: क्षणे नष्टे कुतो विद्या — if the moment is wasted, whence knowledge?

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — कणे नष्टे कुतो ________।
questions.explanation: कणे नष्टे कुतो धनम् — if the grain is wasted, whence wealth?

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — यथा हि एकेन ________ न रथस्य गतिः भवेत्।
questions.explanation: With one wheel (एकेन चक्रेण) the chariot cannot move.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन ________ गच्छति धीमताम्।
questions.explanation: कालो गच्छति धीमताम् — the time of the wise passes in poetry and learning (split form: कालः).

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — काले फलति ________।
questions.explanation: The chapter title: good fortune bears fruit in its own time.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — धैर्यशीलस्य कृषकस्य नाम ________ आसीत्।
questions.explanation: The patient farmer of the story is धीरसेन.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — 'वित्तम्' इत्यस्य समानार्थकं पदं ________ इति। (Write the synonym of वित्तम् used in verse 3.)
questions.explanation: वित्तम् and धनम् both mean wealth; verse 3 uses धनम्.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदं पूरयत — कोऽत्र = कः + ________।
questions.explanation: कः + अत्र → कोऽत्र (विसर्ग-सन्धि, अवग्रह marks the lost अ).

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदं पूरयत — शनैर्विद्या = ________ + विद्या।
questions.explanation: The visarga of शनैः becomes र् before the voiced व्.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — 'फलति' इति रूपं ________ लकारस्य अस्ति।
questions.explanation: फलति is present tense — लट् लकार.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — 'कुरु' इति रूपं ________ लकारस्य अस्ति।
questions.explanation: कुरु is the imperative — लोट् लकार.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — 'काले' इति पदे ________ विभक्तिः अस्ति।
questions.explanation: काले is locative singular — 'at the (right) time'.

questions.question: Explain the meaning and significance of the title 'काले फलति सौभाग्यम्', analysing each of its three words.
questions.answer: काले = locative (सप्तमी) of कालः, 'at the (right) time'; फलति = 'bears fruit, ripens' (root फल्, लट्); सौभाग्यम् = 'good fortune, prosperity'. Together: good fortune bears fruit in its own proper time. The significance: success is not denied to the hard-working, but it keeps its own calendar — like a tree that fruits only in season, honest effort must be continued patiently until its time comes.
questions.explanation: Word-by-word analysis plus the seasonal metaphor that governs the whole chapter.

questions.question: Why is the image of a fruiting tree an apt metaphor for human effort and success?
questions.answer: A tree needs years of invisible growth — roots, trunk, leaves — before any fruit appears, and no amount of impatience can hasten its season. Likewise human effort accumulates invisibly (skill, knowledge, reputation) and yields visible results only when the time is ripe. The metaphor teaches both continuous care (watering daily) and patient waiting (not digging up the seed).
questions.explanation: Maps the stages of a tree's growth onto the delayed, cumulative nature of human achievement.

questions.question: Describe how धीरसेन cared for his orchard from planting to harvest.
questions.answer: He planted a hundred mango seeds in his field and every morning watered them, removed weeds and guarded the saplings from animals. When the villagers mocked him he continued calmly. In the drought year, when the wells dried, he carried water daily from a distant river until his hands blistered. In the fifth year the trees blossomed in spring and bore sweet mangoes in summer, which he shared with the villagers and sold in the town.
questions.explanation: The full arc of sustained care: planting, daily tending, endurance in drought, harvest in season.

questions.question: What did चपल do with his seeds, and what was the result?
questions.answer: चपल planted seeds but, being impatient, dug up the soil week after week to see whether the roots were growing. The repeated digging destroyed the seeds; nothing grew, and in anger he abandoned farming altogether.
questions.explanation: His own checking destroyed the crop — the story's example of self-defeating impatience.

questions.question: How did the villagers' attitude towards धीरसेन change from the beginning of the story to the end?
questions.answer: At first they mocked him — 'Fool! For five years there will be no fruit; why labour in vain?' At the end, seeing the orchard laden with sweet fruit and धीरसेन prosperous, they themselves declared 'काले फलति सौभाग्यम्' — good fortune bears fruit in its own time, and only by patience and effort does one become happy.
questions.explanation: The mockers become the ones who pronounce the moral — the story's frame of vindication.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय of the first half of the verse: 'उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहमुपैति लक्ष्मीः दैवेन देयमिति कापुरुषा वदन्ति', and translate it.
questions.answer: अन्वय: लक्ष्मीः उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहम् उपैति। 'दैवेन देयम्' इति कापुरुषाः वदन्ति। Translation: Fortune (Lakshmi) approaches the industrious lion among men; 'it will be given by fate' — so say (only) cowards.
questions.explanation: Subject लक्ष्मीः, object उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहम्; the quoted इति clause belongs to कापुरुषाः.

questions.question: Explain the verse 'शनैः पन्थाः शनैः कन्था शनैः पर्वतलङ्घनम्...' — list its five items and state its unifying idea.
questions.answer: The five items achieved slowly are: पन्थाः (a long road is covered), कन्था (a patched garment is stitched), पर्वतलङ्घनम् (a mountain is crossed), विद्या (knowledge is gained) and वित्तम् (wealth is earned). The unifying idea: every great accomplishment is a sum of many small steps — शनैः शनैः, only gradually — so one must neither hurry nor despair at slow progress.
questions.explanation: Each image is a large task decomposed into countless small acts.

questions.question: What does the verse 'क्षणशः कणशश्चैव विद्यामर्थं च साधयेत्' teach about time and wealth?
questions.answer: Knowledge must be gathered moment by moment (क्षणशः) and wealth grain by grain (कणशः). A wasted moment can never be recovered for learning, and a wasted grain never for wealth — so both time and resources must be used and saved in their smallest units.
questions.explanation: The rhetorical questions क्षणे नष्टे कुतो विद्या / कणे नष्टे कुतो धनम् drive the point home.

questions.question: Explain the relation between दैव (fate) and पुरुषकार (human effort) as taught by the verse 'यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण न रथस्य गतिर्भवेत्...'.
questions.answer: The verse compares life to a chariot that needs two wheels. दैव — fate, circumstance, timing — is one wheel; पुरुषकार — one's own effort — is the other. Just as a chariot cannot move on a single wheel, fate alone cannot deliver success without effort. Neither wheel is sufficient by itself: the wise person supplies unstinting effort and lets time/fate supply the season, exactly as धीरसेन watered his trees and waited for the fifth year.
questions.explanation: Fate and effort are complementary, not competing — the chapter's philosophical core.

questions.question: Contrast how the wise and the foolish spend their time according to 'काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन कालो गच्छति धीमताम्...'.
questions.answer: The time of the wise (धीमताम्) passes in the delight of poetry and learned works (काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन) — in study, reflection and refined enjoyment. The time of fools (मूर्खाणाम्) passes in vice (व्यसनेन), sleep (निद्रया) or quarrel (कलहेन). The hours are the same; only their filling differs.
questions.explanation: The verse's point is the use of time, not its quantity.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: उद्योगी, कापुरुषः, पौरुषम्, वित्तम्, कलहः.
questions.answer: उद्योगी = industrious person; कापुरुषः = coward, mean man; पौरुषम् = manly effort, personal exertion; वित्तम् = wealth; कलहः = quarrel.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary from the verses on effort and the use of time.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: क्षणः, कणः, कन्था, धीमताम्, व्यसनम्.
questions.answer: क्षणः = a moment; कणः = a grain, particle; कन्था = patched garment, quilt; धीमताम् = of the wise (genitive plural); व्यसनम् = vice, addiction.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary from the verses on gradual progress and the use of time.

questions.question: What does the story teach about how to respond to mockery and discouragement?
questions.answer: धीरसेन neither argued with the mockers nor abandoned his work. He answered calmly — 'the tree fruits in its own season; I wait with faith and do not give up effort' — and let the eventual harvest reply for him. The lesson: meet ridicule with quiet perseverance; results, arriving in their season, silence mockery better than words.
questions.explanation: The story's social lesson: steadiness under discouragement.

questions.question: Apply the chapter's teaching to a Class 12 student preparing for board examinations. Use at least two verses in your answer.
questions.answer: The student should study like धीरसेन farms: a fixed portion daily, continued through dull months, trusting the exam season to reveal the fruit. 'क्षणशः कणशश्चैव विद्यामर्थं च साधयेत्' — knowledge is built moment by moment, so short daily revisions beat last-night cramming; a wasted क्षण cannot be recovered. 'शनैः पन्थाः शनैः कन्था' — the syllabus, like a mountain, is crossed step by step. And 'उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहमुपैति लक्ष्मीः' warns against trusting luck or 'expected questions': fortune in the examination hall approaches the industrious, not the fatalist.
questions.explanation: Direct application of the verses to steady exam preparation versus cramming and luck.

questions.question: Why is impatience self-defeating? Answer with reference to चपल's behaviour.
questions.answer: Impatience demands visible proof of progress before the process is complete. चपल dug up his seeds weekly to check the roots, and that very checking destroyed them. Growth — of seeds, skills or savings — happens invisibly and is disturbed by constant interference; the impatient person thus destroys the process whose results he is anxious to see.
questions.explanation: Interference born of anxiety kills the hidden growth it wants to verify.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद and name the sandhi: (a) पुरुषसिंहमुपैति (b) कालो गच्छति (c) कोऽत्र.
questions.answer: (a) पुरुषसिंहमुपैति = पुरुषसिंहम् + उपैति — the final म् joins the following vowel. (b) कालो गच्छति = कालः + गच्छति — विसर्ग-सन्धि (ः → ओ before voiced ग्). (c) कोऽत्र = कः + अत्र — विसर्ग-सन्धि; the अवग्रह (ऽ) marks the elided अ.
questions.explanation: Three joins from the verses, each split and named.

questions.question: Identify the समास and give the विग्रह: (a) पुरुषसिंहः (b) शुभाशुभम् (c) पर्वतलङ्घनम्.
questions.answer: (a) पुरुषसिंहः — उपमित कर्मधारय; विग्रह: पुरुषः सिंहः इव ('a man like a lion'). (b) शुभाशुभम् — द्वन्द्व; विग्रह: शुभं च अशुभं च ('good and bad'). (c) पर्वतलङ्घनम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष; विग्रह: पर्वतस्य लङ्घनम् ('the crossing of a mountain').
questions.explanation: Three compound types from the chapter with their standard dissolutions.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति of each word: काले, दैवेन, मूर्खाणाम्, यत्ने.
questions.answer: काले — सप्तमी (locative), 'at the right time'; दैवेन — तृतीया (instrumental), 'by fate'; मूर्खाणाम् — षष्ठी बहुवचन (genitive plural), 'of fools'; यत्ने — सप्तमी, part of the locative-absolute phrase यत्ने कृते.
questions.explanation: Four case-forms drawn directly from the verses.

questions.question: What is the सति-सप्तमी (locative absolute)? Explain it using 'यत्ने कृते यदि न सिध्यति कोऽत्र दोषः'.
questions.answer: सति-सप्तमी is a construction in which a noun and its participle both stand in the सप्तमी (locative) to express an attendant circumstance — 'when/while X being done'. In यत्ने कृते, यत्ने (effort) and कृते (having been made) are both locative: 'when effort has been made'. The line then means: if, effort having been made, success still does not come, what fault is there? The construction compresses a whole 'when...' clause into two words.
questions.explanation: Definition plus worked example — the chapter's flagship senior-secondary construction.

questions.question: Name the लकार of each verb form: फलति, कुरु, साधयेत्, वदन्ति.
questions.answer: फलति — लट् (present, 3rd sg.); कुरु — लोट् (imperative, 2nd sg.); साधयेत् — विधिलिङ् ('one should acquire'); वदन्ति — लट् (present, 3rd person plural).
questions.explanation: The three लकाराः that carry the chapter's verbs.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'दैवं निहत्य कुरु पौरुषमात्मशक्त्या यत्ने कृते यदि न सिध्यति कोऽत्र दोषः'.
questions.answer: Setting fate aside, perform manly effort with your own strength; if, when effort has (truly) been made, success does not come, what fault is there (in you)? — i.e. honest effort is always blameless, whatever the outcome.
questions.explanation: निहत्य (ल्यप् gerund) = having set aside; यत्ने कृते is the locative absolute; कोऽत्र दोषः is a rhetorical question.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'धीरसेनः शान्तः एव उत्तरम् अददात् — वृक्षः स्वकाले एव फलति। अहं श्रद्धया प्रतीक्षे, उद्योगं च न त्यजामि इति।'
questions.answer: Dhirasena gave his answer quite calmly: 'A tree bears fruit only in its own season. I wait with faith, and I do not give up effort.'
questions.explanation: स्वकाले = in its own time; श्रद्धया = with faith (instrumental); प्रतीक्षे = I wait; न त्यजामि = I do not abandon.

questions.question: Retell the story of धीरसेन and चपल in your own words (8-10 sentences) and state its moral.
questions.answer: In the village of Sukshetra lived a farmer named Dhirasena. Deciding to raise a mango orchard, he planted a hundred seeds and tended them every morning — watering, weeding and guarding them from animals. His neighbour Chapala also planted seeds, but impatience ruled him: week after week he dug up the soil to check whether roots were forming, and by that very digging destroyed his seeds; angry, he gave up farming. The villagers mocked Dhirasena for labouring five years with no fruit in sight, but he replied calmly that a tree fruits only in its own season and that he would wait with faith without abandoning effort. In the third year a drought struck and the wells dried, yet he carried water daily from a distant river until his hands blistered. In the fifth year the trees blossomed and bore sweet mangoes. He shared the fruit with the villagers — even with Chapala — sold the surplus in the town and prospered. The villagers themselves then declared: काले फलति सौभाग्यम्. Moral: patient, sustained effort ripens into good fortune at the right time, while impatience uproots its own success.
questions.explanation: Complete narrative arc: planting, contrast with चपल, mockery, drought, harvest, moral.

questions.question: Explain the verse 'उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहमुपैति लक्ष्मीः...' fully: give its अन्वय, शब्दार्थ of the key words, translation, and its central teaching.
questions.answer:
अन्वय: लक्ष्मीः उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहम् उपैति। 'दैवेन देयम्' इति कापुरुषाः वदन्ति। (त्वं) दैवं निहत्य आत्मशक्त्या पौरुषं कुरु। यत्ने कृते यदि न सिध्यति, (तर्हि) अत्र कः दोषः?
शब्दार्थ: उद्योगिनम् = the industrious; पुरुषसिंहम् = lion among men; उपैति = approaches; कापुरुषाः = cowards; निहत्य = having set aside; पौरुषम् = manly effort; आत्मशक्त्या = with one's own strength; यत्ने कृते = when effort has been made; कोऽत्र दोषः = what fault is there?
Translation: Fortune approaches the industrious lion among men; only cowards say 'it will be given by fate.' Set fate aside and act with your own strength; if effort honestly made does not succeed, what fault is there?
Central teaching: prosperity follows enterprise, not passive waiting. Fatalism is branded cowardice; a person's whole duty and power lie in effort, and when effort is honestly made, even failure carries no blame — so there is never a reason for idleness.
questions.explanation: The four-part verse treatment (अन्वय, शब्दार्थ, translation, भाव) expected at senior-secondary level.

questions.question: 'Patience without effort is idleness; effort without patience is impatience.' Evaluate this statement in the light of the chapter, citing the story and at least two verses.
questions.answer: The chapter holds patience and effort together as inseparable halves of one virtue. Patience alone — sitting and trusting दैव — is exposed by the verse उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहमुपैति लक्ष्मीः: those who wait for fate to give are कापुरुषाः, cowards, and the chariot verse (यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण) shows that destiny without the second wheel of पुरुषकार cannot move at all. So patience that does not work is mere idleness. Effort alone, without patience, is dramatized by चपल: he worked — he planted, he dug — but his refusal to wait for the season destroyed his own seeds. Effort that demands instant results interferes with hidden growth and defeats itself. धीरसेन embodies the correct union: daily unbroken work (watering through the drought) joined to calm waiting for the fifth year ('वृक्षः स्वकाले एव फलति'). The verse शनैः पन्थाः शनैः कन्था generalises this: all great things are done step by step, so steady action and patient time-keeping are one discipline, not two. The statement is therefore fully consistent with the chapter's teaching.
questions.explanation: Evaluation question requiring synthesis of the story and verses into a single thesis.

questions.question: Write a character sketch of धीरसेन and चपल, showing how their names mirror their natures and how each illustrates one half of the chapter's theme.
questions.answer: धीरसेन ('he whose army is steadiness', from धीर = patient, firm) is long-sighted, disciplined and calm. He plans a five-year project, works at it every morning, answers mockery without anger, and in drought multiplies rather than abandons his labour, carrying river water until his hands blister. His patience is active, not passive — he waits while working. चपल ('the restless one') mirrors his name equally: he wants weekly proof of progress, cannot tolerate the invisible phase of growth, digs up his own seeds, and when the inevitable failure comes, responds with anger and quits farming altogether. धीरसेन illustrates the positive half of the theme — काले फलति सौभाग्यम्, fortune ripens in its season for the patient worker; चपल illustrates the negative half — impatience destroys the very roots of one's fortune. Between them the story turns an abstract proverb into two recognisable human types, inviting the student to choose which name to deserve.
questions.explanation: Names as character keys; each farmer personifies one half of the moral.

questions.question: Write a note on the सन्धि and समास phenomena found in this chapter, giving at least four sandhi splits and three compounds with their विग्रह.
questions.answer:
सन्धि: (1) पुरुषसिंहमुपैति = पुरुषसिंहम् + उपैति — final म् joins the following vowel; (2) कालो गच्छति = कालः + गच्छति — विसर्ग-सन्धि, ः → ओ before voiced ग्; (3) शनैर्विद्या = शनैः + विद्या — विसर्ग → र् before voiced व्; (4) कोऽत्र = कः + अत्र — विसर्ग-सन्धि with अवग्रह marking the elided अ; (5) क्षणशश्चैव = क्षणशः + च + एव — विसर्ग → श् before च, then च + एव → चैव (वृद्धि); (6) यथा ह्येकेन = यथा हि + एकेन — यण्-सन्धि, इ → य् before ए.
समास: (1) पुरुषसिंहः — उपमित कर्मधारय; विग्रह: पुरुषः सिंहः इव, 'a man like a lion'; (2) शुभाशुभम् — द्वन्द्व; विग्रह: शुभं च अशुभं च; (3) पर्वतलङ्घनम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष; विग्रह: पर्वतस्य लङ्घनम्; (4) अनावृष्टिः — नञ्-समास; विग्रह: न आवृष्टिः, 'absence of rain'. These forms show how the chapter's own lines supply a complete grammar drill.
questions.explanation: Systematic collection of the chapter's joins and compounds with names and dissolutions.

questions.question: Write a grammar note on the verb forms and case-constructions of the chapter: identify the लकार of फलति, कुरु, साधयेत्, भवेत् and वदन्ति; explain the gerunds खनित्वा and निहत्य; and explain the construction यत्ने कृते.
questions.answer:
लकाराः: फलति and वदन्ति are लट् (present tense — फलति 3rd singular, वदन्ति 3rd plural); कुरु is लोट् (imperative 2nd singular of कृ, 'do!'); साधयेत् and भवेत् are विधिलिङ् (optative — 'one should acquire', 'there would be').
Gerunds: both mean 'having done X'. खनित्वा ('having dug') takes the suffix क्त्वा because the root खन् has no prefix. निहत्य ('having set aside') takes ल्यप् because its root हन् carries the prefix नि; similarly आनीय (आ + नी) and विक्रीय (वि + क्री) in the story.
यत्ने कृते: a सति-सप्तमी (locative absolute) — the noun यत्ने and participle कृते both stand in सप्तमी to express circumstance: 'when effort has been made'. The whole line यत्ने कृते यदि न सिध्यति कोऽत्र दोषः therefore means: if success does not come even when effort has been made, what fault is there?
questions.explanation: Consolidates the chapter's लकार, क्त्वा/ल्यप् and locative-absolute material in one answer.

questions.question: Compose five simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) on धैर्य (patience) and उद्योग (effort), and give the English meaning of each.
questions.answer:
1. उद्योगेन एव कार्याणि सिध्यन्ति। (Only by effort are tasks accomplished.)
2. धैर्यं विना सफलता न भवति। (Without patience there is no success.)
3. छात्रः प्रतिदिनं किञ्चित् किञ्चित् पठति। (The student reads a little every day.)
4. वृक्षः स्वकाले एव फलति। (A tree bears fruit only in its own season.)
5. अहं फलस्य प्रतीक्षां कुर्वन् उद्योगं न त्यजामि। (Waiting for the fruit, I do not give up effort.)
Together the sentences say: work daily, be patient, and trust the season — the chapter's teaching in one's own words.
questions.explanation: Creation task using chapter vocabulary (उद्योग, धैर्य, स्वकाले, फलति, त्यजामि) in simple लट् sentences.

questions.question: Show how the five verses of the chapter together build up the single theme काले फलति सौभाग्यम्, stating the specific contribution of each verse.
questions.answer: Each verse supplies one pillar of the theme. (1) उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहमुपैति लक्ष्मीः establishes WHO receives fortune: the industrious, not the fatalist — effort is the precondition. (2) यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण balances this: effort and destiny are two wheels of one chariot, so results also need their season — effort cannot skip time. (3) शनैः पन्थाः शनैः कन्था describes HOW the waiting period is filled: by small steps, since every great thing is completed gradually. (4) क्षणशः कणशश्चैव sharpens the step-size to its smallest unit: moments and grains, none of which may be wasted, because lost time can never fruit. (5) काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन कालो गच्छति contrasts the two ways the same passing time can be spent — learning versus vice, sleep and quarrel — showing that time ripens fortune only for those who fill it well. Read together: work steadily (1), respect the season (2), advance step by step (3), waste no moment (4), and fill time worthily (5) — and सौभाग्य will fruit in its काल, exactly as धीरसेन's orchard did.
questions.explanation: Synthesis question: maps each verse onto one component of the chapter's single argument.

questions.question:
गद्यांशं पठित्वा उत्तरत — 'तस्य प्रतिवेशी चपलः नाम अपरः कृषकः आसीत्। सः अपि बीजानि अरोपयत्, किन्तु सः अधीरः आसीत्। सप्ताहे सप्ताहे सः भूमिं खनित्वा पश्यति स्म — मूलानि वर्धन्ते न वा? इति। एवं पुनः पुनः खननेन तस्य बीजानि नष्टानि अभवन्।'
(a) चपलः कीदृशः आसीत्? (b) सः सप्ताहे सप्ताहे किं करोति स्म? (c) तस्य बीजानि केन नष्टानि? (d) अस्मात् अंशात् कः बोधः?
questions.answer: (a) चपलः अधीरः (impatient) आसीत्। (b) He dug up the soil week after week to see whether the roots were growing (भूमिं खनित्वा मूलानि पश्यति स्म). (c) His seeds were destroyed by his own repeated digging (पुनः पुनः खननेन). (d) Lesson: impatient interference with a growing process destroys it — growth needs undisturbed time.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the चपल passage: character, action, cause of loss, and moral.

questions.question:
गद्यांशं पठित्वा उत्तरत — 'तृतीये वर्षे ग्रामे अनावृष्टिः अभवत्। कूपाः शुष्काः जाताः। तथापि धीरसेनः प्रतिदिनं दूरस्थायाः नद्याः जलम् आनीय वृक्षान् असिञ्चत्।'
(a) तृतीये वर्षे किम् अभवत्? (b) धीरसेनः जलं कुतः आनयत्? (c) 'तथापि' इति पदं किं सूचयति?
questions.answer: (a) In the third year there was a drought (अनावृष्टिः) and the wells dried up. (b) He brought water from a distant river (दूरस्थायाः नद्याः). (c) तथापि ('even so, nevertheless') signals that despite the hardship he did not stop — it marks his unbroken perseverance.
questions.explanation: The drought passage: the crisis, the response, and the force of तथापि.

questions.question:
श्लोकं पठित्वा उत्तरत — 'उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहमुपैति लक्ष्मीः दैवेन देयमिति कापुरुषा वदन्ति । दैवं निहत्य कुरु पौरुषमात्मशक्त्या यत्ने कृते यदि न सिध्यति कोऽत्र दोषः ॥'
(a) लक्ष्मीः कम् उपैति? (b) के 'दैवेन देयम्' इति वदन्ति? (c) श्लोकः अस्मान् किं कर्तुम् आदिशति? (d) 'कोऽत्र दोषः' इति प्रश्नस्य आशयः कः?
questions.answer: (a) लक्ष्मीः उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहम् उपैति — fortune approaches the industrious lion among men. (b) कापुरुषाः (cowards) say it. (c) The verse commands: set fate aside and perform manly effort with your own strength (दैवं निहत्य आत्मशक्त्या पौरुषं कुरु). (d) The rhetorical question means that if effort has honestly been made and success still does not come, no blame attaches to the doer — honest effort is always faultless.
questions.explanation: Verse-based comprehension covering subject, speakers, command and rhetorical close.

questions.question:
श्लोकं पठित्वा उत्तरत — 'शनैः पन्थाः शनैः कन्था शनैः पर्वतलङ्घनम् । शनैर्विद्या शनैर्वित्तं पञ्चैतानि शनैः शनैः ॥'
(a) श्लोके कानि पञ्च वस्तूनि उक्तानि? (b) 'शनैः' इत्यस्य कः अर्थः? (c) श्लोकस्य मुख्यः सन्देशः कः?
questions.answer: (a) The five: पन्थाः (road), कन्था (patched garment), पर्वतलङ्घनम् (mountain-crossing), विद्या (knowledge), वित्तम् (wealth). (b) शनैः = slowly, gradually, step by step. (c) Message: all great accomplishments are completed only by steady, gradual progress — never in one leap.
questions.explanation: List, word meaning and message of the शनैः verse.

questions.question:
श्लोकं पठित्वा उत्तरत — 'यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण न रथस्य गतिर्भवेत् । एवं पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति ॥'
(a) रथः केन विना न चलति? (b) श्लोके दैवं कस्मै उपमितम्? (c) श्लोकस्य तात्पर्यं लिखत।
questions.answer: (a) The chariot does not move without its second wheel (एकेन चक्रेण न गतिः — with only one wheel there is no motion). (b) दैव (destiny) is compared to one wheel of the chariot, पुरुषकार (human effort) being the other. (c) Purport: destiny alone cannot bring success; only when human effort joins it — as the second wheel — does life's chariot move.
questions.explanation: The simile's mapping: two wheels = fate + effort; one alone is motionless.

questions.question:
श्लोकं पठित्वा उत्तरत — 'काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन कालो गच्छति धीमताम् । व्यसनेन च मूर्खाणां निद्रया कलहेन वा ॥'
(a) धीमतां कालः केन गच्छति? (b) मूर्खाणां कालः कैः गच्छति? (c) उभयोः तुलनया कः उपदेशः लभ्यते?
questions.answer: (a) The time of the wise passes in the delight of poetry and learned works (काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन). (b) The time of fools passes in vice, sleep or quarrel (व्यसनेन, निद्रया, कलहेन). (c) Teaching: time flows equally for all; wisdom lies in filling the same passing hours with study and worthy pursuits rather than letting them drain away.
questions.explanation: Comparison verse: identical time, opposite fillings, hence the counsel on time-use.

questions.question:
Read the situation and answer: Ananya begins Class 12 in April. She makes a plan — one hour of Sanskrit daily, finishing each chapter's exercises in the week it is taught. Her friend Riya laughs: 'Board exams are in March! Why start now? I will study in February.' In January Riya panics at the size of the syllabus, while Ananya calmly begins her second revision.
(a) Which character of the chapter does each girl resemble, and why? (b) Which two verses from the chapter best describe Ananya's method? (c) What advice from the chapter would you give Riya in January?
questions.answer: (a) Ananya resembles धीरसेन — steady daily effort begun long before the 'season', continued without anxiety; Riya resembles चपल and the villagers — she postpones, mocks the early worker, and panics when the season arrives. (b) क्षणशः कणशश्चैव विद्यामर्थं च साधयेत् (knowledge gathered moment by moment) and शनैः पन्थाः शनैः कन्था (great tasks completed step by step); उद्योगिनं पुरुषसिंहम्... also fits, since Ananya trusts effort rather than luck. (c) Advice to Riya: stop lamenting lost time (क्षणे नष्टे कुतो विद्या — wasted moments cannot be recovered), begin steady daily work at once with her own strength (दैवं निहत्य कुरु पौरुषम् आत्मशक्त्या), and proceed chapter by chapter (शनैः शनैः) rather than attempting everything in one leap.
questions.explanation: Transfers the story's two characters and three verses onto a modern study scenario.

questions.question:
Read the situation and answer: Two friends start small businesses. Arjun opens a tea stall, keeps regular hours daily, saves a little every week, and slowly gains loyal customers over three years. Vikram opens a shop, but seeing no profit after two months, changes the business — thrice in one year — and finally quits, saying 'my fate is bad.'
(a) Evaluate Vikram's statement 'my fate is bad' in the light of the chariot verse. (b) Which practice of Arjun matches कणशः saving? (c) State the chapter's teaching that covers both cases.
questions.answer: (a) By the chariot verse (यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण...), दैव succeeds only when joined to sustained पुरुषकार. Vikram never gave any venture its season — he removed the effort-wheel repeatedly, so blaming fate alone is unjustified; his failure is of patience, not of destiny. (b) Arjun's habit of saving a little every week matches कणशः — wealth gathered grain by grain (कणे नष्टे कुतो धनम्). (c) The covering teaching: काले फलति सौभाग्यम् — sustained effort, continued patiently through the unrewarding early period, bears fruit at the right time; impatient switching uproots the seed before its season.
questions.explanation: Business scenario testing the fate-versus-effort analysis and the grain-by-grain principle.

questions.question:
Read the line and answer the grammar questions — 'दैवं निहत्य कुरु पौरुषमात्मशक्त्या यत्ने कृते यदि न सिध्यति कोऽत्र दोषः'
(a) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of पौरुषमात्मशक्त्या and कोऽत्र. (b) Which प्रत्यय does निहत्य carry, and why that one? (c) Name the construction यत्ने कृते.
questions.answer: (a) पौरुषमात्मशक्त्या = पौरुषम् + आत्मशक्त्या (the final म् joins the following vowel आ); कोऽत्र = कः + अत्र (विसर्ग-सन्धि; the अवग्रह ऽ marks the elided अ). (b) निहत्य carries ल्यप्, because the root हन् has the prefix नि — prefixed roots take ल्यप् instead of क्त्वा for the gerund. (c) यत्ने कृते is a सति-सप्तमी (locative absolute): noun and participle both in the locative, meaning 'when effort has been made.'
questions.explanation: One verse line yielding sandhi, gerund-suffix and locative-absolute questions together.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer — 'धीरसेनः शान्तः एव उत्तरम् अददात् — वृक्षः स्वकाले एव फलति। अहं श्रद्धया प्रतीक्षे, उद्योगं च न त्यजामि इति।'
(a) 'फलति' — कः लकारः, कः पुरुषः? (b) 'श्रद्धया' — का विभक्तिः, कः अर्थः? (c) 'उद्योगम्' — का विभक्तिः, किमर्थम्?
questions.answer: (a) फलति is लट् लकार (present tense), प्रथमपुरुष (third person) singular — 'it bears fruit'. (b) श्रद्धया is तृतीया (instrumental) singular of श्रद्धा — 'with faith'. (c) उद्योगम् is द्वितीया (accusative) singular, because it is the direct object of the verb न त्यजामि ('I do not abandon effort').
questions.explanation: Story-line grammar: tense, instrumental of manner, and accusative object.
